solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Plunders fishing boats leaving Malta behind

indicators.note: to leave something is to go on without it, so a letter is dropped from the word
completes the phrase about leaving something behind, reinforcing that a letter is left out

parts.note: smacks are single-masted fishing boats
M is the international vehicle code for Malta

explanation.surface: Raiders ransack a fishing fleet and sail off, leaving the island of Malta in their wake.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the M out of SMACKS to get SACKS; 'behind' just completes the phrase 'leaving Malta behind'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, a verb from the old pillaging sense of the word.

clue.text: Embroidery done by a wicket keeper?!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a raised style of needlework
second meaning, playful: a cricket wicket keeper's labour is at the stumps

explanation.surface: A cricketer behind the stumps somehow turns out a piece of fancy needlework.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the wicket keeper stands behind the stumps (the three upright sticks) and puts batsmen out by stumping them; the answer is also a raised style of seventeenth-century embroidery.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumpwork is a genuine type of raised, padded needlework popular in Stuart England.

clue.text: A discount arranged for Guardian

indicators.note: things arranged are set out in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone has fixed up a price reduction for a reader of the Guardian newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on Guardian suggests the newspaper, but it is simply a keeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodian is a keeper or protector, which is what a guardian is.

clue.text: Briefly swab his lip and tongue

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so each of the following words loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quick instruction to dab someone's lip and tongue, as a nurse might.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of the three words is docked: SWA + HI + LI. 'Tongue' looks like part of the mouth-cleaning scene but means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Swahili is a Bantu language of East Africa, and tongue is a standard word for a language.

clue.text: Land Peter tilled for one of our neighbours

indicators.note: tilled soil is broken up and turned over, so the letters are churned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Peter ploughed his field to help out the family next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neighbours' suggests the people next door, but here it is our neighbours in the solar system.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars, nicknamed the Red Planet, is one of Earth's planetary neighbours.

clue.text: Turn and run over art benefactor

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
Henry Tate, the sugar magnate, founded the Tate gallery

explanation.surface: A list of things to do: take a turn, go for a run, and look over a patron of the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Tate gave his collection to found the Tate Gallery in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate is to turn round on an axis, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Move policeman's house

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, and the possessive adds S
a lodge is a small house

explanation.surface: An instruction to relocate the home of a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge something is to shift it from its fixed position, so to move it.

clue.text: Tract of arable land originally for rent

parts.note: a lea is a stretch of open land or pasture

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: first letter of the word
to let a property is to rent it out

explanation.surface: A notice advertising a plot of farmland that was first put up for rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tract' looks like an area of land to go with the arable land, but it is a pamphlet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tract is a short pamphlet, typically religious or political, which is a kind of printed leaflet.

clue.text: Northern French city dropping lecturer's material

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern

indicators.note: in a down entry dropping means sinking lower, so one letter slides down a place in the word

parts.note: Lyon is a major city in France
names the letter that moves: L is the abbreviation for lecturer, already present in the city's name

explanation.surface: A city in the north of France sheds one of its university lecturers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' suggests the lecturer is removed, but in a down entry it means the letter sinks one place lower in the word instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fibre used to make fabric, so it is a material.

clue.text: Under-Secretary's supporting bird book

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting part holds up from below, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
US is the abbreviation for Under-Secretary

explanation.surface: A government under-secretary is propping up a book about birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus is one of the epistles of Paul and so a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: International courier's sharp with pretentious person

parts.note: UPS (United Parcel Service) is an international courier company
tart means sharp-tasting

explanation.surface: A parcel delivery firm is curt with a self-important customer.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is someone newly risen in status who behaves arrogantly, a presumptuous social climber.

clue.text: Try to consume every vegetable

indicators.note: consuming something takes it inside, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: to have a shot is to have a try
every and all are synonyms

explanation.surface: Advice to a fussy eater: attempt to eat each of your vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consume' sits naturally with vegetables, but it is the signal to put one word inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small mild onion, a vegetable of the allium family.

clue.text: Regularly backing corrupt expert

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the kept letters are read in the opposite direction
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Someone keeps supporting a crooked specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro, short for professional, is an expert at something.

clue.text: Start home before King enters

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: something that enters goes inside, so the letter is placed within the word

parts.note: as in ten to six, meaning ten before six
R is the abbreviation for Rex, king

explanation.surface: Get back to the house before the monarch arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: IN + T(R)O: the king's letter goes inside the word for before.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is an introduction, the opening section or start of a piece of music or writing.

clue.text: Tracks Vikings heading off to pursue sovereign

indicators.note: with its head cut off the word loses its first letter
to pursue is to follow behind, so this piece is placed after the other

parts.note: a sovereign is a pound coin, abbreviated L from libra
the Vikings who raided England were called Danes

explanation.surface: Viking raiders set off in pursuit of a king, following his tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign was an old British gold coin worth a pound; the pound sign comes from L for libra.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanes are narrow roads or paths, the same as tracks.

clue.text: Source of cast-iron probed by current government

indicators.note: a probe goes into something, so these letters are pushed inside the other word
metal that is cast is poured into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange
I is the symbol for electric current
G is an abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: An inquiry by the present government into where some cast iron came from.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast-iron' reads as one word, but the hyphen hides an anagram signal and its fodder; OR(IG)IN.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the point where something begins, which is its source.

clue.text: Report of your on-line name rejected for access to computer network

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the letters are read backwards
a report is something heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: in a non-rhotic British accent your and yaw sound alike
E for electronic, as in e-mail, plus a tag, a name or handle

explanation.surface: A news item says your internet username was refused when you tried to log on.
explanation.walkthrough: YAW + ETAG, all read backwards. Without the R sound, as most English people say it, your rhymes with saw.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateway is a node that connects one computer network to another, providing access to it.

clue.text: Heard comedian complain on the radio about European booze …

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the two sound-alike words go around a letter
heard means we only go by what the ear catches, so a sound-alike spelling is used

parts.note: a wit is a comedian, and whit is a word that sounds the same
E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: on the radio we only hear words, so a sound-alike spelling is wanted

parts.note: to whine is to complain

explanation.surface: A comic is heard grumbling on air about the European drinks trade.
explanation.walkthrough: The two sound-alike words wrap around the European letter, which lands at the join. The ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: White wine is an alcoholic drink, and booze is slang for alcohol.

clue.text: … that which is already brewed with infusion of old fruits initially

definitions.note: with the ellipsis this continues the previous clue: that which holds booze

indicators.note: brewing mixes and transforms ingredients, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Something ready-made, with an infusion of old fruit added, as in making a fruit beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read on from the previous clue: the answer is a vessel for booze. 'With infusion of' just adds the two initials to the fodder before mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard of ale is a long trumpet-shaped glass holding about two and a half pints, a container for beer.

clue.text: Note a series of musical notes contains a time increase

indicators.note: a word that contains another holds it inside

parts.note: E is a musical note
a scale is an ordered series of notes
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A music lesson: a note, a scale, a time signature, then build up.
explanation.walkthrough: E + SCAL(AT)E: the second 'a' and time go inside the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: To escalate is to grow or intensify, so to increase.

clue.text: Some Africans know heartless tales

indicators.note: with its heart removed the word loses its middle letter

parts.note: ken is Scots for know
yarns are tales

explanation.surface: Some Africans are said to know cruel stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenyans are the people of Kenya in East Africa, so some of the continent's inhabitants.

clue.text: Hangs on when program finishes?

parts.note: an app is a computer program
ends means finishes

explanation.surface: A computer freezes and hangs right as the software shuts down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hangs on' looks like what a frozen program does, but it means attaches at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To append is to add or attach at the end, so to hang something on.

clue.text: North American support for mathematician

parts.note: NA is the abbreviation for North American
a pier is a supporting pillar

explanation.surface: Backing from across the Atlantic for a scholar of numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: John Napier was the Scottish mathematician who invented logarithms.

clue.text: Refrain from seeing holy woman in a French bath

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the woman goes within the bath

parts.note: bain is French for bath
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Advice not to peek at a nun taking a bath in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refrain from' looks like the definition, but 'from seeing' is the link: A + B(ST)AIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to hold back from doing something, so to refrain.

clue.text: Has confidence in modern hospital managers

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the bodies that run NHS hospitals in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone believes in today's health service administrators.
explanation.walkthrough: Since the 1990s British NHS hospitals have been run by bodies called NHS trusts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for having faith in and a plural noun for the bodies administering British hospitals.

clue.text: Role reversal involving married man down on his luck

indicators.note: reversal means turning round, so the word for role is read backwards
to involve is to take in, so the reversed word wraps around a letter

parts.note: an actor's part is a role
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A husband swaps roles at home just when his fortunes are at their lowest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless vagrant, someone who has fallen on hard times.

clue.text: Supplement found in setter's pot?

parts.note: surface reading: an additive tucked into a pot belonging to the setter
setter's reading: the answer, read as a crossword instruction for a down clue, tells you to write the word pot upwards, that is backwards

explanation.surface: An extra helping hidden in the crossword compiler's cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and it is how a setter would write 'reverse the letters of pot' in a down clue: the first word is pot backwards, the second the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-up is an extra amount added to bring something to full, a supplement.

clue.text: Article on the Spanish worker's cooperative

parts.note: art. is the abbreviation for article
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a Spanish labourers' collective.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the article sits on top of the Spanish word.
explanation.definitionFit: An artel was a Russian association of craftsmen or labourers working jointly, a workers' cooperative.

clue.text: Is concerned moving about fields?

indicators.note: letters that move about change places, so they end up in a new order

parts.note: someone who cares is concerned

explanation.surface: A worried person pacing about the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Acres are units of land area, and by extension the word means fields or estates.

clue.text: I may be essential to corporate governance

indicators.note: something essential to a phrase is part of its very substance, so the letters sit inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A company director proclaims that he is indispensable to how the firm is run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' looks like the speaker of the sentence, but it is the definition: the self.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego is Latin for I and in psychology means the self, a person's sense of identity.

clue.text: Flower in taupe growing wild

indicators.note: something growing wild runs out of control, so the letters spread into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A brownish-grey bloom springing up untended in a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The petunia is a popular trumpet-shaped garden flower of South American origin.

clue.text: Fires back without energy and power

indicators.note: going back means running the other way, so the letters are read in reverse
without means lacking, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: to fire someone up is to animate them
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone retaliates with gunfire but has run out of energy and strength.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one E from ANIMATES and read the rest backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is staying power, the strength to keep going.

clue.text: Maybe YouGov head governs half-heartedly

indicators.note: half of the heart goes, so one of the two middle letters is dropped

parts.note: poll is an old word for the head
to steer is to govern or direct

explanation.surface: An opinion-survey firm's boss runs the company without much enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: YouGov is a British online polling company; 'Maybe' says it is just an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollsters are organisations that conduct opinion polls, and YouGov is one example of them.

clue.text: New man heading off to see relative

indicators.note: with its head cut off the word loses its first letter

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new
a piece is a man in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A new arrival sets off to visit a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' means a playing piece, as in chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is the daughter of one's brother or sister, a relative.
